newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo displaced seek refuge with neutral militia.
newsitem.headline: Congo displaced seek refuge with neutral militia.

text.p: Hundreds of Congolese displaced by six days of bloody street battles say they are short of food in a Brazzaville suburb where they have taken refuge under the protection of the neutral "Ninja" militia.

"We have at least 475 people here and we have nothing to give them, many more people are in other places," said Elrigius Mkulima, the curate of the Saint Kizito parish, where the displaced are camped in the classrooms of the church school. "They could bring almost nothing when they fled".

Some came by canoe down the Congo river from northern suburbs of the city, skirting the town centre, where bodies lie in the streets, to arrive in the Bacongo suburb under the control of the "Ninja" militia loyal to Bernard Kolelas.
Others said they had made their way from street to street, sometimes by night, advancing when brief lulls in the fighting allowed them to sneak closer to Bacongo, in the southern part of the city.

"It was terrible, there were bodies all over the place and explosions, and I had to leave everything behind," said one young woman who had fled from the district near the international airport on Friday.

Kolelas, the mayor of Brazzaville, heads a mediation committee which is trying to bring about negotiations between soldiers and ethnic militiamen loyal to President Pascal Lissouba and the "Cobra" ethnic and political militia fighting for ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso.
The fighting was sparked when troops surrounded Sassou Nguesso's house to enforce a ban on private militias in the run up to presidential elections which are scheduled for July 27.

A third appeal for a ceasefire from Kolelas, who is also a presidential candidate, went unheeded on Monday night. The thud of mortars and the crackle of small arms fire could be heard through the night from the town centre.
Bacongo, which was near the heart of militia fighting following disputed elections in 1993 in which at least 2,000 people were killed, has this time been spared the bloodshed in the rest of the city.
Two people died after stray shells fell into the district, but the "Ninjas" patrol the outskirts and the warring sides have not ventured into Bacongo or brought Kolelas's militia into the fighting.
